payload.claim: [host-filed criterion probe] tests/test_intake.py::test_coverage_problems_names_each_negative_claim_that_declares_no_positive_case stayed green with the spec's wrong version 'The negation line placed before the member lines.' applied to saffron/intake.py as an edit. The claim was "`coverage_problems` also returns one line for a criterion whose claim holds a word of `intake.NEGATION_WORDS` and that declares no `positive_case`. The tuple holds exactly `no`, `not`, `never`, `nothing`, `none`, `neither`, `nor`, `without` and `cannot`. A word matches whole and in any case, inside backticks too. The criterion yields one such line however many words match. The line is exactly `criterion {n}: its claim says {word!r} and it declares no positive_case`, where `word` is the first match in the claim, lowercased. The witness drives each word in its own claim, and an upper case and a sentence-initial form, each the only listed word in its claim. One loud claim ends with its word and a full stop. Its quiet claims hold each word inside a longer word, and they yield no line. One quiet claim comes first, one sits among the loud ones, and one comes third from last. A criterion with an undriven member and a negative claim yields the member's line first. The last two criteria hold one negative claim. The first of them declares a `positive_case` and an undriven member, and yields only the member's line. The last declares no `positive_case` and yields the negation line. The witness compares the whole list of lines from the one call.", and the whole `tests` gate stayed green under the edit too.
